| [CLAIM-365](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-365.md) v4 | Frustration residual has a simplex dual | A34 §4 and A35 §3 of the exchange of 2026-10-17, checked. The residual is the smallest worst-case shortfall of the declared local improvements ε_i over updates of size at most r. Minimax for the bilinear problem on two compact convex sets gives the dual over the simplex, so Φ_r > 0 exactly when some λ certifies that no update meets all demands (A34's form). Governance regret Γ is the gap between an actual admissible update's shortfall and Φ_r, and is never negative. For L₁ = (θ − 1)², L₂ = (θ + 1)² at θ = 0, Φ_r = ε for every r. The sharp edge: per A37 it is a cardinal refinement of the ordinal fact ([CLAIM-347](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-347.md)), and its magnitude depends on units (A36 §2D). | Active |

In [CASE-352](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-352.md) the renormalized flow reproduces the law exactly, and nothing trained without the re-whitening does. Without weight decay, unconstrained features and two small ReLU networks grow ω_j exponentially or with log-log slopes of 2.4 to 5.5 and spread them apart, while NC1 stalls: plain gradient flow conserves Σ_T, so ω can diverge only by Σ_W turning singular along the readout directions. With weight decay, ω_j grow, stall, regrow and settle at finite, unequal values, or fall back in an instability. So on this evidence the law is a property of the renormalization A3, and [QUESTION-181](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-181.md)'s answer is "no" for small models; at the scale of Han and colleagues' networks it is untested. | [CLAIM-993](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-993.md) | Barrier set by width, group and path family | What [CASE-385](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-385.md) measured, stated as a finding. In two-hidden-layer ReLU MLPs on a two-cue task, the barrier left after alignment falls with width for every kind of pair. At width 5, pairs that rely on the same cue keep barriers (0 to 0.65 in loss) that overlap those of pairs relying on different cues (0.15 to 0.54), even after an exhaustive search over permutations and rescalings. From width 64, both kinds are connected. Within a width, the barrier falls as the matched units' activations correlate more. Permutations alone leave a barrier between two copies of one function that differ by per-unit rescaling, and quotienting rescaling removes it. A trained curve joins aligned endpoints that the straight line does not, both across the board and in the one flat, poorly connected cell of a load-by-temperature grid, where the accuracy deficit stays. So in this toy, connectedness after alignment is a property of width, of the symmetry group and of the path family, more than of the mechanism. The wording is the assistant's (Claude, in this session); adopting it is the owner's call. | Proposed |
